title: Question (polynomial weak coloring numbers for intersection graph classes)
statement_text: Are the $k$-th weak coloring numbers polynomial in $k$ for the following graph classes: intersection graphs of $t$-thin sets of (a) scaled and translated copies of the same centrally symmetric compact convex object, or comparable axis-aligned boxes; or (b) $b$-ball-like objects for some $b\geq 1$?
context_text: Graphs are finite and simple. For a linear order $\prec$ of $V(G)$ and $k\ge0$, a vertex $u$ is weakly $k$-reachable from $v$ if $u\preceq v$ and some path of length at most $k$ from $v$ to $u$ has all internal vertices greater than $u$, and strongly $k$-reachable if moreover all internal vertices are greater than $v$; $\mathrm{wcol}_k(G)$ (resp. $\mathrm{scol}_k(G)$) is the minimum over $\prec$ of the maximum over $v$ of the number of vertices weakly (resp. strongly) $k$-reachable from $v$. For a finite set $S$ of objects in $\mathbb{R}^d$, the intersection graph has vertex set $S$ and edges between intersecting objects; $S$ is $t$-thin if every point of $\mathbb{R}^d$ lies in the interior of at most $t$ objects ($t=1$: touching representation). An object $v$ is $b$-ball-like if it is compact convex with volume at least $1/b$ times that of a ball of diameter $\mathrm{diam}(v)$; axis-aligned boxes are comparable if for any two of them a translate of one is contained in the other. For these classes, ordering objects by non-increasing diameter gives $\mathrm{scol}_k(G)\le t(2k+1)^d$ in case (a) and $\le bt(2k+2)^d$ in case (b), i.e. polynomial in $k$ for fixed $d,t,b$. Joret and Wood conjectured that polynomial strong coloring numbers imply polynomial weak coloring numbers; Grohe et al. disproved this using subdivisions, but the authors ask whether it still holds for these natural classes. The paper itself answers it: for homothets of a centrally symmetric compact convex object and for $b$-ball-like objects, $\mathrm{wcol}_k(G)\le t\max(1,\lceil\log_2k\rceil)(4k-1)^d\binom{k+t5^d+2}{t5^d+2}$ (resp. a similar bound), which is polynomial in $k$; but touching graphs of comparable axis-aligned boxes in $\mathbb{R}^3$ can have $\mathrm{wcol}_{2k}\ge2^{k+1}-1$, so for comparable boxes the answer is negative. They also show that the dependence on $t$ must be in the exponent in dimension at least $2$.
notes: Stated as a prose question without a labelled theorem environment. Theorem 3 of the paper gives polynomial (in $k$) upper bounds for scaled/translated centrally symmetric objects and $b$-ball-like objects, giving a positive partial answer; Theorem 4(i) shows exponential lower bounds for touching comparable axis-aligned boxes in $\mathbb{R}^3$, giving a negative answer for that subclass.
